start: ^It is Wednesday. The launch is Friday. Maria has sent three messages, Dev has sent one, and Sam has not sent any because he gave up on the booking form last week.
^Maria wants the gallery animation. Dev wants the menu update to take five minutes. Sam needs the booking action to work on a phone.
^Protect the booking path and defer the animation
^Add the animation because Maria asked for it

c-0: ^You write the decision down: booking first, animation only if time allows. Maria is disappointed for one message, then agrees to see the booking flow.
c-1: ^The gallery moves. It looks impressive on your laptop. You have not tested the booking form on a phone yet.
c-2: ^You explain what is still unsafe. Maria does not love it, but she would rather launch once than apologise twice.

test: ^The booking form is the one task every customer will try. The animation is the one nobody needs. The menu is the one Dev will change every Monday.
^Test the three top tasks on a phone and with a keyboard
^Test the happy path in your browser

c-0: ^You book on a 375px screen, tab to the button, submit, and read the confirmation with a screen reader. Two small issues appear; both are fixable tonight.
c-1: ^The desktop happy path works. The phone is still an assumption.
c-2: ^You ship. The dashboard is quiet. The support inbox is not.

decide: ^The site is ready enough to make a decision. The question is what the client is actually buying.
^Delay the launch and fix the booking path

c-1: ^You call Maria, explain the one remaining risk, and move the launch by two days. She agrees when she sees the booking flow working.

ending_solid: ^The site launches. Nobody writes a dramatic review, because nothing breaks. Sam books a table on the bus. Dev changes the menu on Monday without calling you.
^That is the last 20 percent: not more features, fewer surprises.
ending_delayed: ^You move the date. The client is not thrilled, but the booking path works and the animation is documented as a later improvement.
^The launch is smaller and calmer than the promise. It also survives the first week.
ending_fragile: ^ENDING: It looked fine on the laptop
^The launch goes ahead. On a phone, the booking button sits off-screen. Sam tries once, then goes to the cafe up the road.
^The analytics say the site is live. The customer says otherwise.
